 :Judgment:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of 10,50,000/ for the injuries sustained in a Road Traffic accident.

The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 08.07.2018 at about 5.30 pm., the Petitioner was travelling as a pillion rider and the grand father of the Petitioner was riding Passion Pro Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA52H4245 slowly, carefully and cautiously by following traffic rules on the left side of the road on Doddachannavahalli - Thavarekere road, Thyamagondlu Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk, Bangalore Rural District

, at that time, one TATA Nano Car bearing Reg.No.KA02MF2690 driven by its driver came in a rash and negligent manner and with a high speed and dashed against the Petitioner's Passion Pro Motor Cycle and thus caused the accident.
As a result, the Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries to all over the body.

Immediately, after the accident, Petitioner was shifted to V.P.Magnus Hospital,
Nelamangala wherein he was admitted as an inpatient and surgery was done.
He also admitted in SCH 15 4 MVC No.4615/2018 Hemavathi Hospital, Tumkur and he has incurred Rs.3,80,000/ towards medical treatment and other incidental charges.
Due to injuries sustained by the Petitioner, he has suffered mental shock and agony and Permanent disability.
Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and was aged 18 years and was doing part time job and was earning Rs.17,000/ per month and also he is a student.
Respondent No.1 being the RC owner and Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.

In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, Respondents appeared before the Court through their respective Counsels and filed their Objections to the main petition.
SCH 15 5 MVC No.4615/2018 Respondent No.1 in its Objection Statement to the main petition has denied the age, avocation and monthly income of the Petitioner.
Further denied the expenses incurred by the Petitioner for his treatment.
Further contended that, vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA02MF2690 was duly insured with the Respondent No.2.
Hence, he is not liable to pay any compensation to the Petitioner.
On these grounds, Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement to the main petition denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further it has denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the accident and the expenses incurred for the medical treatment.
On these grounds, Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.
On the rival Pleadings my Learned Predecessor has framed the following Issues:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that, he has sustained injuries due to RTA alleged to have been occurred on 08.07.2018 at about 5.30 A.M, on Doddachannavhalli Thavarkere Road, Thyamagondlu Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District, due to the rash and negligent driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA02 MF 2690?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what amount and from whom?
3. What Order or Award?
7. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 13 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13.
Further, he examined SCH 15 7 MVC No.4615/2018 three witnesses as PW.2 to PW.4 and got marked 9 documents as per Ex.P.14 to Ex.P.22 and closed his side evidence.
On the other hand, Respondent No.2 examined one witness as RW.1 and got marked 2 documents as per Ex.R.1 and R.2 and closed its side evidence.
Respondent No.1 did not choose to lead evidence.

8. Having heard the arguments by the learned Counsels for both sides and upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:

Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per the Final Order, for the following :

REASONS 9. ISSUE No.1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that, he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident SCH 15 8 MVC No.4615/2018 that occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Car bearing Reg.No.KA02MF2690 by its driver.
10.

11. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, he got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 13 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13.
He also examined three witnesses as P.W.2 to 4 and got marked 9 documents as per Ex.P.14 to Ex.P.22.
P.W.1 has reiterated the Petition averments in his chief affidavit.

Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.5 are the True copies of FIR with Complaint, Spot Mahazar, IMV report,
Wound certificate and Chargesheet.

Ex.P.6 to 13 are the Discharge summaries, Aadhar card,
Medical bills, Advance Receipts, Prescriptions, 8 Photos with 1 CD, lab report and Xray respectively.

12. Upon going through Ex.P.1 i.e., FIR with Complaint shows that on the Complaint lodged by complainant before SCH 15 9 MVC No.4615/2018 Tyama Gondlu Traffic Police Station, the PSI of the concerned Police Station has registered the case against the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA02MF2690 for the offences punishable under sec. 279, 337 of IPC.
Ex.P.2 is the Spot panchanama which shows that the concerned police had drawn mahazar at the spot in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P.3 is the IMV report which shows that the accident does not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicles.
Ex.P.4 is the Wound Certificate of the Petitioner which shows that the Petitioner had sustained the grievous injuries.

Ex.P.5 is the Certified copy of the Charge sheet which shows that after thorough investigation, the PSI of Tyamagodlu Traffic Police Station has submitted Chargesheet against the driver of the offending car for the offences punishable under Sec. 279, 337 and 338 of IPC r/w Section 187 of IMV Act.
13. Upon going through the Chargesheet i.e., Ex.P8 Column No.17 reads as under:

Ex.P.4 is the Wound Certificate relating to the Petitioner which shows that the Petitioner has admitted in the V.P.Magnus Hospital, on the history of Road Traffic Accident and he had sustained injury of Fracture of Proximal Tibia Right side with Foot Drop.
As per the opinion of the Doctor, the injury is grievous in nature.
15. Ex.P.6 is the Discharge summary which shows that the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient from 08.07.2018 to 11.07.2018.
16. Further, P.W.1 has examined 3 witnesses as PW.2 to PW.4 and got marked Ex.P14 to Ex.P22.
PW.4 is Dr.Nagaraj B.N who has reiterated the injuries sustained by the Petitioner.
17. On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 has examined its Legal Manager by name Ibrahim as R.W.1 and he got marked 2 documents at Ex.R.1 and R.2.
In the cross examination of R.W.1, he admitted that at the time of accident, the policy of the offending vehicle was in force.
Further, he SCH 15 12 MVC No.4615/2018 deposed that, he does not know about pleading guilty and payment of fine by the driver of the offending vehicle before the JMFC Court.

It is pertinent note here that,
after thorough investigation charge sheet has been filed against the driver of the offending vehicle.

18. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the Petitioner has proved the rash and negligent driving of the offending Tata Nano Car bearing Reg.No.KA02MF2690 by its driver and due to the accident the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the 'Affirmative'.
19. Issue No.2:

As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending car by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled Sri. Jayaram.A vs ) Umashanker.G on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32721669/
5 for compensation.
20. In the Petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 18 years.
Further, in the Adhaar card i.e., Ex.P.7, the year of SCH 15 13 MVC No.4615/2018 birth of the Petitioner was shown as 2001.
The accident took place on 08.07.2018.
In all the medical documents, age of the Petitioner is shown as 18 years.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner, as on the date of accident was 18 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.
21. Further, the Petitioner has averred that, he was a student and also part time worker and was earning Rs.17,000/ per month.
But he has not produced any document for his income proof.
Therefore, in the absence of any documentary evidence, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
Since, the accident has occurred in the year 2018 the income of the petitioner is notionally taken at Rs.12,500/ per month for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
24. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the SCH 15 14 MVC No.4615/2018 sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING :
25.
It is stated in the petition that, in the accident, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
As per Wound Certificate i.e., Ex.P.4 issued by the V.P.Magnus Hospital, shows that in the said accident the Petitioner has sustained Fracture of Proximal Tibia Right side with Foot Drop.
26. As per the opinion of the doctor, above said injury is grievous in nature.
27. Having regard to the nature of injury sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.40,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

SCH 15 15 MVC No.4615/2018 II. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
28. Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

III. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID-UP PERIOD:

The Petitioner deposed in his evidence that he has taken the treatment at V.P.Magnus Hospital, Bengaluru.
Upon going through Ex.P.6  Discharge summaries of V.P.Magnus hospital, Bengaluru, which shows that the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient in the said hospital from 08.07.2018 to 11.07.2018.
Therefore, while calculating the total period of which the Petitioner admitted as an inpatient, it comes to 04 days.
30. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may SCH 15 16 MVC No.4615/2018 be considered as two months.

Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.25,000/ under this head (@ Rs.12,500/ per month ).
IV. COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
31.

Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period,
the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.6,000/ (@ Rs.100/ per day) towards attendants charges, Rs.6,000/ towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.6,000/
towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.18,000/ under this head.
SCH 15 17 MVC No.4615/2018 V.COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES :
32. The Petitioner has deposed that he has spent more than 3,80,000/ towards medical expenses and other incidental charges.
In order to prove this fact, he has produced total 118 Medical bills and hospital bills, which is marked at Ex.P.8.
I have gone through the said Medical bills.

The medical bills to the extent of Rs.2,27,877/
are acceptable.
Hence, by rounding off the same, the same to be taken at Rs.2,27,900/.
Hence, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,27,900/ under this head.

VI. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS / COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY:
33.

The Petitioner has stated that due to the injury sustained by him in the accident,
he has suffered permanent disablement and he is not able to do his work as he used to do earlier.
Even in his evidence, P.W.1 has deposed to that effect.

sentences.text: Further, the Petitioner got examined one witness by name Dr. Nagaraj B.N as P.W.4 who has deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a Road Traffic Accident and the treatment taken by the Petitioner.
Further, he has deposed that the Petitioner had disability to the whole body at 28%.
Further, PW.4 got marked examination report and Xray as per Ex.P.21 and 22.
In the cross examination, PW.4 admitted that he has not treated the Petitioner and he has not obtained the opinion of the treated doctors of the Petitioner.
Further, he admitted that the Petitioner does not need further surgery.

Further he admitted that,
fracture of the Petitioner is united.
He has denied the suggestions putforth to him by the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.2.

Hence, by considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that considering the disability of the Petitioner with respect to the whole body at 15% would be just and proper.
As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 18.

With multiplier of 18, income of Rs.12,500/ per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to his whole body at 15%, the loss of future income comes to 4,05,000/ (Rs.12,500/ x 12 =
1,50,000/, Rs.1,50,000/x 18 x15/100 = 4,05,000/).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 4,05,000/ under this head.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
36.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs. 40,000/
2. Loss of amenities Rs. 30,000/
3. Loss of income during the Rs. 25,000/ laid up period 4.
Attendant's charges, Extra Rs. 18,000/ diet, and conveyance SCH 15 20 MVC No.4615/2018 5.

Medical expenses Rs.2,27,900/
6. Loss of Future Income Rs.4,05,000/ Total Rs.7,45,900/
37.
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.7,45,900/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

38. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the Offending Tata Nano Car bearing Sri. Jayaram.A vs ) Umashanker.G on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32721669/
8 Reg.No.KA02MF2690.
In this case, the Respondent No.1 is the owner and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Further, the Respondent No.2 admitted the validity of the Insurance Policy of the offending car.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award amount.
The Respondent No.2, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1, has to SCH 15 21 MVC No.4615/2018 pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
39. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 and 2 , I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of Rs.7,45,900/ along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the Insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and SCH 15 22 MVC No.4615/2018 interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be released to the petitioner by way of E payment and after proper identification.
The remaining 25% award amount shall be deposited as F.D. in the name of the Petitioner in any Nationalized or Schedule bank for a period of three years.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw Award accordingly.
